newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh still assessing crop losses from storm.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh still assessing crop losses from storm.

text.p: Bangladesh agriculture officials said on Tuesday they were still assessing crop losses from Monday's severe cyclonic storm, but they believed the damage would be limited.
"We are still trying to get a full picture. But (we) expect the impact not to be too severe," one official told Reuters.
He said the season's main Boro rice paddy had been mostly harvested and "whatever losses caused by the cyclone would not warrant any emergency situation".
The cyclone blowing from the Bay of Bengal battered the country's vast coastal region, killing hundreds of people and threatening major economic losses.
But Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday her government handled the crisis efficiently.
Officials in Chittagong, one of the areas worst hit by the cyclone, said on Tuesday that crops on 150,000 acres (60,000 hectares) were damaged by strong winds.
"We don't have further details at the moment," one official said, although shrimp farms along the coastline were badly damaged.
Bangladesh earned $265 million from shrimp exports in 1995-96 (July-June).
